ratings.text:
Upright lead,
the many fall in.
ratings.reasons: Matches the picture well (the general brightens, the ranks fall in). But 'Upright lead' is clipped and reads first as an adjective and a noun, even as the metal. 'The many' is stiff. Put the verb first so the instruction is clear, and name the ranks the viewer sees.
ratings.rewrite:
Lead upright,
the ranks fall in.

ratings.text:
High and low talk:
that is peace.
ratings.reasons: Line 1 is 18 characters, the limit. Faithful to the Image, plain, and 'talk' makes a clean pair with 12. It fits the picture of the two trigrams meeting. It defines peace rather than asking something of the viewer, but a newcomer gets the point: peace is contact between high and low.

Fits the picture (they drift apart) and pairs with 11. But it only states the situation. The Image says what to do in it: conserve your character and decline honours and pay. A newcomer learns what standstill is but not what it asks. Keep the 11 parallel and add the ask.
ratings.rewrite:
High and low part:
turn down rewards.

ratings.text:
The one with most
keeps lowest.
ratings.reasons: 'The one with most' leaves 'most' hanging (most what?). 'Keeps lowest' does not match the picture: the yang line stays in third place and steps back and dims, it does not go lowest. Say what the viewer should do and use the picture's own move.

Faithful to line 1 and fits the split and rejoined line. But the break splits the phrasal verb 'Turn / back', and it uses the 'X? Y.' question form, which 51 also uses. Drop the question and keep 'come back', which the picture shows.
ratings.rewrite:
Once you stray,
come back soon.

ratings.text:
Guard your mouth:
food and words.
ratings.reasons: Plain and faithful to the Image (careful with speech, moderate in eating), and the chewing jaw sets it in memory. A newcomer gets the intent at once. The colon form is shared with 11, which is acceptable.

Line 1 is good and matches the strained picture. 'Act now' is vague and sounds like a sales push. It does not say what the act is for. The source supports going forward to relieve the strain, so name that: shore the beam up.
ratings.rewrite:
The beam sags.
Shore it up now.

ratings.text:
Light holds
to what is right.
ratings.reasons: The light/right rhyme is sing-song, and 'holds to' is weaker than the source's 'clings', which is the whole name of the hexagram. It is a statement about light, not something asked of the viewer. Name the fire in the picture and make it an instruction.
ratings.rewrite:
Like fire, cling
to what is right.

ratings.text:
Remove the wrong
in the open.
ratings.reasons: Covers half the cited Judgment (proclaimed at court) but leaves out the other half, 'resorting to arms is not supported', which is the hexagram's main caution. Without it, 'remove the wrong' can read as a purge. Add the no-force part.

ratings.text:
Check a bad start
while it's small.
ratings.reasons: Plain and faithful to line 1 and Wang Bi ('check' is the metal brake). It fits the picture closely: the rising yin is met and held by the line next to it, then settles. A newcomer gets the intent right away. Both lines are 17 characters.

Faithful to the Image (use fear to examine yourself). But the break splits 'Look / at', and the 'X? Y.' form repeats 24's. With both changed the set has no question lines, and a plain 'when' clause does the same work.

ratings.text:
Empty of self,
firm at the core.
ratings.reasons: Line 2 matches the picture (the 2nd and 5th lines brighten) and the Tuan. 'Empty of self' reads as mannered and faintly spiritual, and a newcomer will not connect it to sincerity or trust. Line 1 of 61 gives a plain form: no hidden aim. The open centre in the picture then reads as nothing hidden.
ratings.rewrite:
No hidden aim,
firm at the core.
